subject: Chemistry
title: Supercooled Water: Instant Ice
description: Learn Supercooled Water: Instant Ice in one minute.

hook.text: Pour perfectly still water below 0°C and it stays liquid. Tap the bottle and it freezes instantly.

buildup.text: Water needs a nucleation site—a tiny impurity or vibration—to start forming ice crystals.

discovery.text: Without a nucleus, water molecules can't organize into ice. They remain liquid well below freezing.

twist.text: Trees use antifreeze proteins to survive winter. They prevent nucleation inside their cells.

climax.text: Understanding supercooling helps us preserve organs for transplant and predict ice formation on aircraft.

punchline.text: Liquid below zero. One tap and it freezes solid. Nucleation is the trigger.

quiz.question: Why does supercooled water stay liquid below 0°C?
options: It lacks a nucleation site to start crystal formation
It contains dissolved salt that lowers the freezing point
The container insulates it from the cold

details.summary: Supercooled water remains liquid below zero degrees Celsius because it lacks nucleation sites for ice crystal formation. When disturbed by a tap, impurity, or ice crystal, the water freezes almost instantly in a visually dramatic chain reaction of crystallization.
details.whyItMatters: Supercooling is critical in atmospheric science where supercooled droplets cause aircraft icing. It also has applications in cryopreservation, food science, and materials engineering.
takeaways: Pure water can stay liquid well below zero without nucleation sites
A small disturbance triggers rapid crystallization throughout
Supercooled clouds cause dangerous aircraft icing conditions

faq.question: How cold can water be supercooled before it freezes spontaneously?
faq.answer: Ultra-pure water in laboratory conditions has been supercooled to about minus 48 degrees Celsius before spontaneous freezing occurs. In practical conditions, impurities typically trigger freezing at much higher temperatures, around minus 10 to minus 20 degrees.

faq.question: Why does tapping a supercooled bottle trigger instant freezing?
faq.answer: The tap creates pressure changes and microscopic disturbances that provide nucleation sites where ice crystals can begin forming. Once a crystal forms, it propagates rapidly through the supercooled liquid because the water is already below its freezing point.
